incidents-bot: ALERT — elevated 5xx + STS throttling observed from AWS eu-central-1 affecting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Spike started ~T-6m. AlertID=aws-sts-euc-197650.

Maya (oncall-sre): seeing 502/503 bump on api.redwood.com in eu-central-1, auth failures in logs: `sts:AssumeRole` returning 500/429. Pinged AWS status already.

Alex (eng-runtime): confirmed. Token fetch latency from STS >5s, retries piling up. Continuous-batching queues increase, tail latency spikes.

Priya (support-lead): any idea on customer impact? Which accounts in Dedicated?

Sam (platform): Dedicated pools in eu-central-1: pool-dc-1, pool-dc-3. Both reporting higher token error rates. Mapped top 5 accounts: acme-inc, finlytics, beta-startup, infra-co, edu-open.

Maya (oncall-sre): immediate mitigation steps I started: 1) disabled eu-central-1 routing for non-regional sticky traffic (canary off). 2) Enabled forced fallback to eu-west-1 for token procurement via routing-policy v3. 3) Applied temporary rate-limit on internal token refreshes: `token_refresh_rate=0.6`

Alex (eng-runtime): +1. Pushed policy change: `routing.policy.region_preference = [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]` (rolled back to prefer eu-west). Batching controller reduced max_batch_size to 32 for affected hosts to avoid long tail.

incidents-bot: NOTE — automatic rollback protections paused for affected routes to allow manual control.

Priya (support-lead): preparing customer comms. Which customers are actively seeing 5xx vs degraded latency? Sam?

Sam (platform): acme-inc and finlytics: 5xx spike. Others mostly latency. Marking acme-inc high priority.

Jen (product-ops): creating status page draft: "Investigating — third-party auth provider (AWS STS) in eu-central-1 causing elevated errors. We are routing requests to eu-west-1 and monitoring. Some customers may see increased latency." Will post in ~10m.

Maya (oncall-sre): Quick health checks run:
```
# sample checks
curl -sS https://api.redwood.com/health | jq .region
# eu-central tokens error snippet
2026-03-15T02:17:03Z ERROR sts: AssumeRole failed status=500 requestId=abcd-1234
```

Alex (eng-runtime): Logs show token clients retrying with exponential backoff but hitting STS throttling. Suggest turning on short-lived local token cache TTL to 15s for affected region as emergency (from default 60s). Will deploy config in 2 mins.

Maya (oncall-sre): Deployed local token TTL=15s to reduce STS calls per host. Monitoring token request rate now.

incidents-bot: AWS Status updated: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ — message: "Investigating issues with STS in eu-central-1" (link).

Priya (support-lead): Support play: notify acme-inc + finlytics engineers with workaround — set region=eu-west-1 endpoint for API calls if they can accept cross-region latency. Draft message ready.

Sam (platform): Also enabled model fallbacks for Hosted API route: switch heavy models -> compact variants for eu-central traffic to reduce compute pressure while auth stabilizes. Route change ID=rb-197650-01.

Alex (eng-runtime): Deployed circuit-breaker for token fetch paths: after 5 failed attempts within 1m mark host degraded and serve cached token if available.

Maya (oncall-sre): Impact summary so far: Hosted API 5xx rate peaked ~8% of requests in eu-central over 5m window. Dedicated pools acme-inc & finlytics experiencing request failures and elevated latency. No data breach. No model corruption.

Jen (product-ops): ETA for full recovery depends on AWS fix. If STS returns to normal we'll see errors drop within token cache TTL (~15-60s). Preparing escalation to customer success for enterprise calls.

Priya (support-lead): Sent first batch of customer messages to acme-inc and finlytics. Included workaround + link to status page.

Maya (oncall-sre): Handoff to night oncall in 25m. Leaving runbook and run commands below.

--- Handoff checklist (Maya -> NightOncall) ---
- Current state: routing preferentially to eu-west-1; token TTL=15s; circuit-breaker active; model fallback active.
- What to watch: token_request_rate, sts_5xx_rate, hosted_5xx_rate, dedicated_pool_errors.
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood/obs/dashboards/incident/1976509876
- Runbook snippets: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/token-proxy -n infra` ; `redwoodctl routing set-region-priority --route hosted-api --regions eu-west-1,eu-central-1`
- Pager escalation: if hosted_5xx_rate > 5% for >10m escalate to SRE lead (call tree).

Alex (eng-runtime): leaving logs & diffs: commit d3f9a7 -> config: local_token_ttl=15; routing-policy v3 applied.

incidents-bot: ACTION — incident created in pagerduty: PD-INC-1976509876, current status: acknowledged.

Maya (oncall-sre): Handing off now. NightOncall, please acknowledge and post updates every 30 mins until resolved.

Sam (platform): I'll keep monitoring Dedicated pool health and will be reachable if re-routing needs manual capacity adjustments.

Priya (support-lead): Support will follow up with affected accounts and update tickets.

NightOncall (ack): acknowledged — taking over. Summary noted. First check completed: sts_5xx_rate down to 3.2% (15m window). Continuing monitoring.

Maya (oncall-sre): thanks — leaving thread. If anything spikes call me. :phone: :heavy_check_mark:
